senses.definition: A conventional phrase used to start a letter or conversation or otherwise to acknowledge a person's arrival or presence.
examples: It's polite to begin a letter with a greeting, but this practice is less common in email.

senses.definition: (uncountable) The action of the verb to greet.

quotes.text: I had occasion […] to make a somewhat long business trip to Chicago, and on my return […] I found Farrar awaiting me in the railway station. He smiled his wonted fraction by way of greeting, […], and finally leading me to his buggy, turned and drove out of town.
quotes.reference: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter II, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:

senses.definition: present participle and gerund of greet
